claim: Kasteel Prins de Merode is a private residence of Prince Simon de Merode, normally closed to the public, opened exceptionally for Kerstmagie in December and Historalia productions every two years in summer.
quote: Het kasteeldomein wordt uitzonderlijk opengesteld in het kader van Kerstmagie elk jaar in december

claim: An English landscape park of 12 hectares surrounds the castle with ponds connected to the moat, and a larger 60-hectare formal French-style park lies across the Nete river featuring a rectangular reflection pond.
quote: An English landscape park of 12 hectares surrounds the castle. The ponds in the park are connected with the moat of the castle. Additionally, across the Nete river there is a larger formal park (60 hectares) in the French tradition with a rectangular pond

claim: Jean Philippe Eugène de Merode (1674-1732) designed the park in front of the castle and built its large lake around 1710 after visiting Versailles, creating a mix of styles unique in Belgium.
quote: designed the park which extends in front the Castle... built a large lake in the Castle's parkland... a mix of styles [that] is unique in Belgium

claim: The Kasteelfeesten — the principal day on which the private castle and park open to the public — runs the first weekend of July (45th edition Saturday 6 and Sunday 7 July), with ~6,000 visitors, ~100 exhibitors, tickets 8 euros and free entry for under-14s.
quote: Op zaterdag 6 en zondag 7 juli vindt de 45ste editie van de Kasteelfeesten plaats op het kasteeldomein de Merode... Toegangstickets kosten 8 euro. Kinderen jonger dan 14 jaar mogen gratis binnen.

claim: Kerstmagie is an annual December event where visitors tour the castle for about an hour following a Christmas storyline guided by costumed characters, with a winter bar and stalls run by local clubs in the courtyard.
quote: an annual event for all ages... wandering through the castle for approximately one hour, encountering costumed characters and festively decorated spaces

claim: Kasteel Jeanne de Merode, the neo-Gothic 1909-1911 'New Castle' that has served as Westerlo's town hall since 1972, is freely accessible during municipal opening hours and during regular exhibitions; groups can book guided tours via Toerisme Westerlo.
quote: accessible during the opening hours of the municipal administrative services and during exhibitions that regularly take place

claim: The De Merode walking network counts roughly 700 km of waymarked paths across three provinces, billed as the most popular walking area in Flanders, and connects to the Hagelandse Heuvels, Demer en Dijle, Kempense Netevallei, Grote Netewoud and Limburg networks.
quote: 700 kilometers of walking paths across 3 provinces in Flanders, making it 'the most popular walking area in Flanders.'

claim: Landschapspark de Merode straddles three provinces (Antwerp, Limburg, Flemish Brabant) and nine municipalities — Aarschot, Diest, Geel, Herselt, Hulshout, Laakdal, Scherpenheuvel-Zichem, Tessenderlo-Ham and Westerlo — covering ~1,500 ha of forest and farmland once owned by the de Merode family.
quote: Landschapspark de Merode lies on the border of three provinces: Antwerp, Limburg, and Flemish Brabant. The Landscape Park extends over nine municipalities: Aarschot, Diest, Geel, Herselt, Hulshout, Laakdal, Scherpenheuvel-Zichem, Tessenderlo-Ham and Westerlo

claim: The De Merode walking network passes between junction points 12 and 13 along the Grote Nete bank, offering scenic exterior views of the castle and its mirror pond (spiegelvijver) for visitors who cannot enter the grounds.
quote: Between walking junction points 12 and 13 of the de Merode walking network, hikers can walk along the Grote Nete riverbank with scenic views of 'het kasteel en de spiegelvijver'

claim: Westerlo's Sint-Lambertuskerk is a basilical cross church whose choir dates to 1416 with a nave from the 16th century and tower rebuilt in 1760; it was restored 1890-1904 with a private chapel and burial chapel for the de Merode family, and protected as a monument in 1976.
quote: Het koor van de neogotisch herbouwde kerk dateert uit 1416, het schip uit de zestiende eeuw, de toren werd in 1760 herbouwd... van 1890 tot 1904 werd de kerk gerestaureerd en uitgebreid met een privékapel voor gravin Jeanne de Merode en een grafkapel voor de familie de Merode

claim: The Grote Markt in Westerlo is an elongated triangular Frankish-origin square that hosts a weekly Wednesday morning market with around one hundred stalls selling fresh food, household goods and textiles.
quote: Het marktplein van Westerlo heeft de vorm van een langgerekte driehoek... Elke woensdagvoormiddag worden de Grote Markt en de omliggende straten ingenomen door een honderdtal marktkramers

claim: Westerlo's village shopping concentrates along Gravin de Merodestraat and Boerenkrijglaan, with fashion, gift and flower shops, hair salons and convenience stores within walking distance of one another.
quote: De handel concentreert zich langs de Gravin de Merodestraat en de Boerenkrijglaan, waar mode-, cadeau- en bloemenzaken, kapsalons en buurtwinkels op wandelafstand van elkaar liggen.

claim: Three major cycle networks (Kempen, Hageland and Limburgse Kempen) cross Landschapspark de Merode, and the dedicated mountain-bike network covers 231 km linking through to Hageland and Kempen.
quote: Landschapspark de Merode is crossed by 3 major cycling networks: Kempen, Hageland, and the Limburgse Kempen, and mountain bikers can enjoy 123km of mountain bike trails. The mountain bike network of de Merode is 231 km long
